newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks close out week at another record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks close out week at another record.

text.p: Swiss shares shook off early doldrums to score another record close on Friday, extending Thursday's gains above 4,600 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
Dealers said U.S. Februrary jobs data in the second half of the session helped Swiss shares bounce back from early lows. "It was surprising how fast the market recovered," one dealer said.
The outlook remained generally good but indices were likely to track developments on Wall Street closely, one trader noted.
The SMI ended up 33.7 points, or 0.73 percent, at 4,638.9 points, narrowly below an all-time intraday high of 4,640.9.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 12.79 points, or 0.44 percent, to 2,938.44, also a record close.

Volume was described as heavy but below that of the past few days. Most shares rebounded in the second half. Particularly financials held up well, defying pressure from sagging futures on government bonds, one trader said.

Novartis registered stock led the actives list, powering ahead 1.83 percent, or 32 francs, to 1,779. Roche certificates, which during the sessions were as much as 220 francs lower, closed up 30 francs at 12,540.
Among banks, UBS bearer shares, which were under pressure on Thursday, were up 11 francs to 1,338. SBC and CS Group also firmed.
Nestle eased slightly, giving up two francs to 1,639. ABB, Holderbank, Sulzer, Clariant, Swiss Re and Baloise were also among the blue-chip losers.
Second-tier Valora saw heavy volume, soaring nine francs to 337 after reporting it would float a division and pay out part of the share capital to shareholders.
